children: in an all-stock transaction that has an implied equity value of approximately $3B, the company said on Monday, sending shares up 3.6% in early trading. EROK shares up 15%.
The combination is expected to broaden TPL’s access to key Permian subregions and enhance its ability to serve customers throughout Texas and New Mexico.

TPL’s core competencies across land and water management enable commercial upside across this larger footprint while preserving its high-margin, capital-light business model focused on maximizing durable free cash flow, the company said.

"Given the confidence in free cash flow expected to be generated by the combined business, TPL intends to return more cash to shareholders with increased share repurchases and regular dividend per share growth."

In terms of Permian land footprint, the company will own approximately 1.0 million fee surface acres, plus an additional 105,000 acre dedication. Approximately 37,600 future undrilled well locations lie within five miles of the pro forma combined acreage, which is expected to provide a long runway of future development activity.

Additionally, the deal is expected to expand TPL’s water infrastructure footprint to approximately 1.5 million barrels per day of aggregate non-potable water sourcing and produced water treatment, a 49% pro forma increase. Combined water storage capacity is expected to total approximately 68 million barrels, a 79% increase.
The transaction is expected to be accretive to TPL’s estimated 2027 free cash flow per share before synergies, while preserving its high-margin financial profile.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, pro forma adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow margins were approximately 83% and 60%, respectively. The pro forma combination maintains TPL’s strong balance sheet and net cash position as of September 30, 2026.

This financial position is expected to provide flexibility to expand capital returns and fund growth investments. In connection with the transaction, TPL's Board of Directors approved an increase in the company's share repurchase authorization to $500M.
management has also identified approximately $45M in expected annual run-rate benefits, including $20 million of corporate cost savings and $25 million of revenue opportunities.

title: Texas Pacific Land to buy EagleRock in ~$3B deal, expanding Permian land and water reach; EROK shares rally 15%
